findings.rationale: An AWS security group is configured to allow unrestricted ingress from 0.0.0.0/0 on TCP port 22, exposing administrative SSH access to the internet.
An IAM role is configured to allow assumption by an entity that can be reached via the ingress chain, violating least privilege.
The internet-facing security group is chained with an assumable IAM role, creating a direct path from external exposure to identity compromise.
An overly permissive IAM policy is chained with a publicly accessible S3 bucket, enabling an attacker with compromised identity to expose sensitive data.

findings.rationale: An IAM policy grants broad wildcard permissions ('*') for actions and resources, severely violating the principle of least privilege.
